own_solution.law: The equilibrium mean collision frequency per molecule is z = n πd²〈v_rel〉 = √2 n πd²√(8kT/(πm)), with n = P/(kT). Using m = 28u = 4.650e-26 kg gives z = 5.59e9 s^-1. An added pressure of 33 kPa at unchanged temperature raises the pressure to 113 kPa, giving z = 7.90e9 s^-1.
assumptions: The requested rate is the equilibrium ensemble-average collision frequency for one molecule.
The stated hard-sphere ideal-gas model applies, with collision cross section πd².
The separate gas cylinder has no connection to the vessel.
The added 33 kPa denotes an increase in the vessel's pressure at the stated temperature.

T209B.regime: Bulk equilibrium gas with vessel dimensions much larger than the mean free path; 12 cm greatly exceeds the approximately 85 nm mean free path.

T6ADA.regime: Bulk equilibrium gas with vessel dimensions much larger than the mean free path; 12 cm greatly exceeds the approximately 85 nm mean free path.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: TE094 and T62EC replace the specified 33 kPa with an unquantified 'small amount', so the added-nitrogen variants do not preserve the required number and unit.

notes: The base physics and the individual sentence-conditioned answers are well posed under the usual interpretation of collision frequency as a mean rate. Volume cancels because N/V = P/(kT). Earlier runs have no effect on the stated current equilibrium. The invalid verdict concerns the required numerical matching of sentence variants: TE094 versus TA9C7 and T62EC versus T7923 omit 33 kPa. Those omissions do not change their disconnected roles.
